package_info.why_malicious: This report does not analyze a specific malicious package or provide any code samples. Instead, it discusses general supply chain attack scenarios (e.g., event-stream, Webmin, Browserify typosquatting) and how SLSA and Sonatype products can help mitigate such threats. No direct evidence or code from a malicious package is presented.

behavioral_signatures: Component provenance does not match expected source repository
Dependency tree includes components with unknown or unverifiable origin
Package names closely resemble popular packages (typosquatting)
Sudden changes in package behavior or content between versions
file_indicators: Packages with names similar to popular libraries (e.g., browserify vs. browserifyy)
Components with missing or mismatched provenance metadata
network_indicators: Packages downloaded from untrusted or unofficial mirrors
Artifacts retrieved from sources not matching the official repository
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for components whose provenance (origin, uploader, repository) does not match the expected source. Flag packages with names similar to popular libraries (typosquatting). Use behavioral analysis to detect sudden or suspicious changes in package content or behavior, especially in dependencies. Employ repository firewalls and component intelligence tools to automatically quarantine or block suspicious packages before they enter the build or release pipeline. Regularly review dependency trees for unverifiable or unexpected components.
